title: Existence of the normalized degreewise evaluation map
statement: For any commutative ring A and cochain complexes P,Q on the one-object bottom-topology ringed site [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map], and any integer n, there exists a morphism from the degree n of Tot(Hom(P,A[0]) tensor Q) to Hom(P,Q)^n satisfying the signed evaluation normalization [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-degree-condition]. No boundedness, finiteness, or projectivity hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1), expanded chain-level evaluation; Tag 0ATK, lemma-base-change-evaluation-map, clause (1)

proof.text: Identify internal Hom sections at the unique point with A-linear maps, reusing pointHomEquiv and pointLift from RingHomExtensionDegrees. The section tensor comparison is a linear equivalence: the bottom-topology sheafification unit is invertible, as is tensorObjIsoSheafification. Form the linear evaluation of each degree-r dual by composing the chosen Hom projection with pointHomEquiv and the degree-zero single-complex identification. Apply Mathlib dualTensorHom after tensoring this linear evaluation with the identity, multiply by (r*s).negOnePow, and transport Q^s to Q^(-r+n). Conjugating by the tensor comparison and internal-Hom equivalence constructs evaluation_block and proves its prescribed pure-tensor formula by cancellation of the equivalences.

Use the chosen limiting fan of Hom(P,Q)^n, reusing ringHomComplex_isLimit from PerfectRingDualTermFlat. For a tensor summand (r,s), put evaluation_block in coordinate -r and zero in every other coordinate, transporting along p=-r. Fan.IsLimit.lift assembles the coordinate maps. HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorDesc assembles all tensor summands into the desired degree map. Its inclusion equation and Fan.IsLimit.fac give both off-diagonal vanishing and the diagonal signed evaluation formula, exactly PerfectRingHomTensorDegreeCondition. No finite-support, flatness, projectivity or boundedness theorem is used.
